done_when: forge merge enable changes an existing merge key wherever and however forge.toml writes it (indented, single- or double-quoted, with a comment) and adds one only when there is none, and the file still parses; a test covers each form

findings.body: Forge accepts `merge = """human"""`, but this regex replaces only the first two quotes, leaving invalid TOML, so enable refuses instead of changing the key. The new test at tests/test_fix_forge_merge_enable_adds_a_second_merge_k.py:36 expects that refusal rather than a successful command-level edit. A double-quoted key containing a TOML escape, such as `"mer\u0067e"`, also parses as `merge` but is missed by the regex; inserting another key then creates a duplicate. The parser in src/forge/repo.py:205 uses tomllib, and its merge validation at line 138 accepts the resulting `human` value. Cover these valid forms through `forge merge enable` and change the existing key.
findings.title: Not done: forge merge enable changes existing merge keys in valid quoted forms

findings.body: The search treats any line beginning with `[` as the first table, even when that line is inside a multiline TOML string. For example, a valid root `test = """\n[options]\n"""` followed by `merge = "human"` makes `top` stop before the existing merge key. Enable inserts a second root key and then refuses the duplicate. `test` is an accepted string setting in src/forge/repo.py:132 and is not restricted to one line by its validation at line 281. Locate actual TOML tables so this valid placement can be edited.
findings.title: Handle a table-looking line inside a multiline config string

why: forge merge enable adds a second merge key when forge.toml writes it indented or quoted, which breaks the file
